name: Rubaya mining sites named in PE76 / former PE4731
selection_reason: S/2025/446 para 113 lists the sites worked under AFC/M23 inside PE76 and the revoked PE4731. These IPIS sites match that list.
notes: Spelling matches we assumed: Bundjali = Bunjari; Luwowo/Gasasa = Luwowo/Nyange and Kasasa. Kashaki (03062) is about 11 km east of the D sites and is the weakest match. Excluded: 03285 'D2 Bibatama' (coordinates about 37 km south of the Rubaya sites, likely a data error). Listed by the UN but no IPIS match: Muderi, Muchacha (Rubaya), Nyambisi, Luoo. The IPIS site 'Muchacha' is in Mambasa, Ituri, and is unrelated. The UN satellite annex places the main coltan hill in permit PE16159, attributed to SAKIMA (S/2026/466 annex 67), so permit numbers have changed; do not select on PE numbers alone.

name: Rubaya mining area: other IPIS sites within 4 km
selection_reason: S/2024/969 para 56 says the entire mining area around Rubaya is held. SMB's licence was 30.5 km2 (Amnesty p12), a circle of about 3.1 km radius; 4 km adds about 1 km for coordinate error. Centre is the mean of the D-site coordinates.
notes: Radius is our inference. Masisi sites only; sites already in area_rubaya are removed.
method: S/2024/969 para 56 says the entire mining area around Rubaya is held. SMB's licence was 30.5 km2 (Amnesty p12), a circle of about 3.1 km radius; 4 km adds about 1 km for coordinate error. Centre is the mean of the D-site coordinates.

name: Lomera (Luhihi), Kabare: nearest IPIS gold sites
selection_reason: S/2025/858 paras 59-60 place the Lomera site at Luhihi and say M23 took de facto control of mining in the area. Lomera itself is not in IPIS: it dates from late 2024 or Jan 2025. The 4 km radius catches the only IPIS gold sites nearby.
notes: These four sites are neighbours visited in 2022-23, not Lomera. Radius is our inference. Centre is Luhihi village (OSM node 1160970919), not the mine; Amnesty puts the mine on the Lake Kivu shore.
